name: Dysprosium
occurrence: Found in low concentrations within monazite and xenotime ores; took Boisbaudran over 30 fractional-crystallization attempts to isolate.
majorUses: Additive in neodymium magnets to improve heat resistance
Nuclear reactor control rods (high neutron absorption)
notableCharacteristics: Its name comes from the Greek 'dysprositos', meaning 'hard to get', reflecting how difficult it was to separate from other rare-earths.
whyHere: Its ten 4f electrons give dysprosium strong magnetic properties that remain stable at higher temperatures than neodymium's alone, which is exactly why a small amount of it is blended into neodymium magnets used in electric vehicle motors.
didYouKnow: Dysprosium's name literally translates to 'hard to get' in Greek — its discoverer needed more than 30 rounds of a tedious separation process just to isolate a usable sample.
genZNote: Named 'hard to get' and really committed to the bit — took over 30 tries to even isolate. Worth it though, EV motors need it.
